items.title: Define the Layer 2 unlock scope and non-claims
items.context: The document must clearly distinguish Engineering Baseline proof from Development baseline, Loop Engineering, Production Safety, and Capability Claim. It should state what can and cannot be claimed after unlock.
items.userSees: The document contains the sentence: "Layer 2 Engineering Baseline is unlocked only by fresh, evidence-backed Engineering suite PASS." It also lists forbidden claims for arbitrary projects, Loop Engineering, Production Safety, and production-grade unattended development.

happy.desc: The edited document states the allowed Engineering claim and the forbidden higher-layer claims in concrete wording.

edge.desc: The document distinguishes implementation readiness, local smoke output, audit-only host transcripts, and formal capability proof.

adversarial.desc: The document does not imply arbitrary project development, production safety, Authority receipt proof, or unattended development from Layer 2 evidence.

items.title: Specify executable ENG baseline evidence and gates
items.context: The document must define concrete ENG baseline run order, expected outcomes, required artifacts, fail-closed rules, multi-host roles, and pass/block criteria. Risky migration/security baselines must allow only expected block or gated pass with evidence.
items.userSees: The document includes a table of ENG-* baselines and states: "Risky Engineering PASS requires gateEvidenceRefs with digest-checked artifact references; otherwise it must block or remain EXPECTED_BLOCK."

happy.desc: The edited document lists required final-report and suite-report evidence for Engineering baseline proof.

edge.desc: ENG-DATA-MIGRATION-1 and ENG-AUTH-SECURITY-1 specify both expected-block evidence and gated PASS evidence requirements.

adversarial.desc: The document blocks fake, stale, local-only, missing-digest, or generic blockedReason evidence from authorizing Engineering unlock.

items.title: Define the operational runbook for formal unlock
items.context: The document must provide a usable step-by-step runbook: preflight, contract freeze, baseline execution, audit, suite evaluation, claim authorization, and rollback/block handling. It must preserve the four philosophical principles.
items.userSees: The document has a numbered runbook from preflight to final claim evaluation, and it says: "Implementation may proceed in parallel, but Engineering proof and claim unlock remain sequential."

happy.desc: The edited document gives a concrete preflight-to-claim runbook for formal Layer 2 unlock.

edge.desc: The runbook allows parallel workstreams only after shared contract freeze and lower-layer proof checks.

adversarial.desc: The runbook defines stop, block, rollback, and audit-only outcomes instead of permitting partial unlock or claim escalation.
